looksRight: Round 1, Pete's hood: it now lies on his shoulders below the neck. Nothing crosses his mouth in table-wide (202.26), band-end and counted-in (206.05, 207.02, 207.69), they-look (211.13 to 213.22), chair-in (213.51) or the-meal (225.62, 227.94).

Round 1, Sibyl at larry-and-sibyl: from 220.65 to 222.78 her face is turned down, crown foremost, toward her plate and away from Larry, through both 'It's my house.' and 'It's still the rule.'. It reads at 640 by 360.
Round 1, OPEN during the cook-in-back push: the neon is whole (59.07, 59.88) and then absent (61.58, 61.98). No fragment of the word is left at a frame edge.
Round 1, the busker after walk-past: he is full size at 104.02, and at 107.04 he and his case are small at the far left, still standing. He gets smaller as he goes.

Goodnight is reframed: Dee, Larry, Al and Eppy are in the shot with no head behind Larry's, from the cue (230.42) through every line and the hold (232 to 248). Four heads, Sibyl out of frame. Nothing behind him moves to the front, and the light does not change.

Studio work lamp: it is now a reflector hung above his head with a faint cone to the pool by the desk (0.05 to 21.66). It is well clear of his mouth in the wide, the desk close and the ask medium. It puts no word, letter or mark on screen, and it no longer reads as a microphone.

Snow: it starts during the cross (167.77) as sparse flakes, thickens through the last block (170.35 to 175.98) and runs through the door (176.96 to 201.16) and the table window. It stays as flakes the whole way, never a blizzard. No flake mass covers a face, the WALK sign (164.69, 165.35, 167.77), the warm top window or the watcher in it.

Kitchen hatch: the plate on the pass and the steam rising past the hatch frame read at phone size (59.88 to 88.15). The cook's figure is still clear of them. On cook-slows he still leans in close over the board (83.14 to 85.3) while the room keeps bobbing, and in watch-the-cook (86.53) Larry and the cook are both in frame.
The crossing from still-red (161.29) to walk-sign: DON'T WALK in red, then WALK in green, both plain; nobody looks up at the change; the road is empty.

His door: the watcher stands at the left of the warm top window from apartment-door to back-to-us and is gone before the door opens at let-in (198.6, 199.41). The warm light falls across the snow and across him (200.76). The listen-door hold (181.96 to 184.39) changes nothing but the snow.

The table is still six in the same seats in every shot: Pete, Hy, Al, Dee, Eppy and Sibyl in order, seen as Sibyl at the head, then Eppy, Al, Dee, Hy and Pete. Seven heads appear only in table-wide and they-look, and four or fewer everywhere else. The gold chair, the second chair, the dish uncovered after the cut and the bowl are as passed in round 1. No glass is raised, and nothing changes the light at they-look or goodnight.
Envelope, coat, scarf and cardigan continuity is unchanged from round 1. The first frame (0.05) is the dark studio with no title card. The last frame (249.68) is black.

Credits: QUOTED is now three centred lines with no hanging separator: 'Pirkei Avot, chapter 2', 'translated by Joseph I. Gorfinkle,' and '"The Sayings of the Jewish Fathers", first published 1913'. The year is 1913 and no edition is named. TOLD FROM is unchanged, and so are the busker 'On the corner' line and the synthesized-voices line.
forTheOwner: Whether the listen holds are heard as us speaking, and whether the coin lands as the tune's missing note. As in round 1, the picture does what was asked and only sound can settle these.
Whether the cook's change of pace, now with steam and a plate beside him, still reads at speed on a phone. In stills it does.
